With no provider set up, the composer's model picker shows the raw id "gpt-5.4-mini" (default provider openai, empty catalogue) and no thinking picker; Kenneth asked for it drawn.
=== expected-errors-tables-confirmed

Kenneth, 2026-11-15, on the two tables shown to him in chat: "This table looks good. Confirmed." The rule in AGENTS.md asks for his yes on every entry and his words in the commit message; these are the words. The code that held the tables was deleted the same day ([[desktop-app-error-reports-default-on]]); copies of the deleted files are in `error-sweep-trial/deleted-build-session-2026-11-15/`.

**Desktop app, failed AI requests** (cause → what the person sees → next step):
- App older than the server serves → "This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts." → Get the new version
- Sign-in ended, or own API key rejected → "Their sign-in has ended, or the API key was rejected." → Sign in again, or update the key
- Out of credits → "They are out of credits." → Get more credits
- Chat larger than the AI service accepts → "The request was too large for the AI service." → none shown today
- Provider or our server limiting speed → "The AI service is rate limited." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider overloaded → "The AI service is overloaded." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider down or unreachable from our server → "The AI service is temporarily unavailable." → Retry
- Provider too slow, or connection stalled → "The AI request timed out." → Retry
- No network → "The AI request could not reach the service." → Check the network, then Retry

**Server, expected answers:**
- Signed out → "Sign in to JusPrin to continue." → Sign in again
- Out of credits → "This message needs N credits; you have M." → Get more credits (the table first shown to him said "You do not have enough credits for this message.", which the server never sent; asked which to keep on 2026-11-15, he took the pick, what the server sends: "Go with your picks for both")
- App too old → "This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts. Get the new version to keep using your account." → Get the new version
- Too many turns a minute, or provider limiting us → "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again." → Wait and retry
- Server's slots for large requests all taken → "JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment." → Retry
- Provider down, overloaded or unreachable → "The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly." → Retry
- Provider too slow → "The model service took too long to answer." → Retry
- Chat or report photos too large → "The request is too large." → New chat, or fewer pictures
- Print report too short → "A report needs a few sentences." → Write more
- Print report has no photo → "A report needs a photo of the printed object." → Add a photo
- Report photo cannot be opened → "That photo could not be read." → Add a different photo
- Print already reported → "This print already has a report." → Nothing

Also confirmed by the same answer: a provider's own "overloaded" event partway through a reply (Anthropic `overloaded_error`, OpenAI `server_is_overloaded`) counts as the "unavailable" entry and is not reported. The server table is in code since 2026-11-15: `web_ent/jusprin/v2/errors.py` `EXPECTED` (commits 057ea6d412, then the credits correction).

The second column is as shown to him: the app column is the build session's description of the sentence, not always the literal on-screen string, so check each against the code when rebuilding. The server's four other answers (invalid_request, unknown_model, method_not_allowed, upstream_error) stay unexpected: "Agreed. Treat them as unexpected errors." Note that at the last commit a provider's 400 or 422 is answered as invalid_request, which is the shape of the 2026-11-14 incident. The designed refusals outside AI requests (81 rows, not 89; `error-sweep-trial/designed-refusals-outside-ai-requests.md`, sorted in `designed-refusals-sorted.md`): on 2026-11-15 Kenneth decided the eleven that are failures with a sentence of their own and no named cause (rows 10, 11, 16, 21, 39, 54, 55, 58, 59, 60, 71) become unexpected errors: "Yes, go with this approach." A session converted 11, 16, 39, 55, 71 (on jusprin-dev in b3eed3bf4b) and asked him whether 10, 21, 54, 58, 59, 60 stay. Asked "Should the six failure sentences that session left alone stay as they are?", he answered the same day: "Yes, keep them". So those six keep their sentences (projects folder unreadable x2, "Signing in didn't finish", another app's settings file unreadable, "hasn't loaded the AI models yet", "The open project couldn't be saved"). The session's new on-screen strings (report rows App / Was doing / Where, the singular forms, the Preferences box text) were put to him in full the same day and he answered: "approved". The other 17 not-on-a-board rows are real named causes, not yet entered or confirmed.

**2026-11-20, three causes from the error-messages brief's "may be the person's to fix" list.** Kenneth, on three "Decision needed" paragraphs: "Go with your picks". Entries:
- Outside AI app's own setup command could not start, or exited with an error (Preferences › BYOAI › Connect… on Claude Code or Codex) → "The setup command failed." + "Copy the command and run it yourself." + Copy button; the command's output stays under Technical output → run the command by hand. Before this, the page hid the message (it equals the diagnostic) and showed only the title.
- Printer renamed or removed while its printer chat is open → the connect call fails and the AI gets "This printer was renamed or removed. Open it again from Printers.", which it words itself → reopen it from Printers. No code change; not run in the app.
- Bambu network plug-in not installed → printer chat notice "Bambu plug-in needed" with Install plug-in (Figma state boards, 4389492239) → install it. His pick also made "installed but fails to load" unexpected, but that pick rested on my guess that reinstalling may not help. Found after his yes: Install plug-in re-downloads (GUI_App::ShowDownNetPluginDlg), which can fix a damaged copy, and on Mac/Linux a missing file also sets NetworkAgent::get_load_error, so the two cases are not reliably told apart. Put back to him the same day; he chose "Keep the notice": both cases keep the notice and Install plug-in, no report, no code change.
=== composer-model-pickers

Branch `claude/composer-redesign` (worktree `JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign`,
on top of `claude/design-token-sync` 76105af26c), uncommitted as of 2026-10-20:
composer redesign, native file picker (`pick_attachment`), and per-chat
provider/model/thinking pickers (`model_choice` capability: `set_chat_model`,
`model_catalog`, `chat_model`).

Design that matters:
- Superseded 2026-11-02, see [[chat-keeps-its-model]]: for now no mid-chat switch.
  The goal recorded here on 2026-10-20 was to switch provider, model and thinking
  level at any point in a chat, like ChatGPT/claude.ai, and the code still allows it.
  Earlier turns replay provider-neutrally (no
  thinking blocks cross turns), so a switch needs no history translation.
- Choice stored per chat as `chatModel` in the project's Agent document;
  absent = default provider's default model.
- An agent handed to the host (constructor, setup, harness mock) counts as
  the default choice's agent. Rebuilding it on the first turn stalled the
  full harness once; host test "a chat's model choice decides the agent each
  turn runs on" guards this.
- Lists: Anthropic GET /v1/models (capabilities → effort levels, adaptive
  only); OpenRouter /api/v1/models?supported_parameters=tools (`reasoning`
  object); OpenAI /v1/models has no capability data, so ModelCatalog.cpp
  guesses (gpt-5*/o* get low/medium/high).

**Live smoke, 2026-10-20 (Kenneth approved using the OpenAI key stored in
~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf for that batch only):**
`agent_live_tests "[models][live]"` passed for OpenAI: 76 models listed,
a one-word reply on gpt-5.4-nano at effort low, then gpt-5.4-mini. Anthropic
and OpenRouter have no stored key and are live-untested. Ask before any
further live run. Open design question: OpenRouter's tool-capable list
is hundreds long (menu scrolls; search or curation undecided).

2026-10-20 later: committed as fe2a30c640; then (uncommitted) the narrow-pane rule
(Composer measures; .composer-choices--narrow hides "Thinking:"), model-menu search
above 12 models (component.fieldSearch token), and the WebKit menu-click fix
[[webkit-click-does-not-focus-buttons]]. Kenneth has since stored an Anthropic key
too; the default provider in his JusPrin2.conf is anthropic.

Merged 2026-10-20 into local jusprin-newui as 1ca65bb087 (unpushed): two commits,
7671e48504 token sync and a8d5fe87a0 composer + search + narrow + click fix
=== chat-keeps-its-model

Kenneth, on the credits board 3b, 2026-11-02: "For now, let's assume that we don't allow users to switch model mid-chat. If I previously said the opposite, you need to update your memory now." He gave no reason, so don't invent one.

This reverses the goal recorded in [[composer-model-pickers]] on 2026-10-20 ("switch provider, model and thinking level at any point in a chat").

**Why:** Kenneth's decision; "for now" means it can come back, so ask before treating it as permanent.

**How to apply:** a chat's tier or model is chosen before its first message, and after that its picker stays in the composer, greyed. There is no "Send with Basic" or "Switch this chat to Basic"; when an Expert message can't be paid the ways forward are buy, subscribe, or a new Basic chat. Still saying otherwise as of 2026-11-02: the app's `Composer.tsx`, where the picker is only disabled while the Agent responds; reconcile it before building. The older pricing and cache plans that allowed a switch within one wire format are retired. The credits boards on the canvas already follow it.

Kenneth on credits board 7a, 2026-11-02: "keep the model /thinking selection design, but greyed out with a tooltip to explain that model can't be changed mid-chat. also explain the credits/msg". So once a chat has a message, both pickers stay in place, greyed, and a tooltip gives the reason and the price (board 2c). This replaces my plain "Expert · 5 credits a message" text; the price per message is now in the menu and the tooltip.
=== live-suite-is-part-of-done

On 2026-10-29 I merged and pushed the chat-history record change (history appended in place, skills kept where they fired) after unit tests, the scripted prompt suite, a request-byte prefix check and a live cache measurement. Kenneth asked afterwards whether I had run live prompt testing for regressions. I had not, and I had not proposed it. He asked whether I should have recognised the need; the answer was yes.

**Why:** the byte checks prove the app sends stable requests and the cache measurement proves the provider caches them. Neither says whether the model still answers each case the way the baseline recorded. The project prompt README already states that changes affecting what the model reads are exercised through the live suite. A reordering of the conversation is such a change even when every byte is "the same content".

**How to apply:** before recommending a merge of any change that alters the bytes the model reads, list the live prompt suite (tests/project_prompt, and tests/printer_prompt when printer flows are touched) as a remaining step and ask Kenneth's approval for the batch in plain words with the cost, per [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]] and [[live-eval-after-only-vs-baseline]]. "Tests pass" in a merge recommendation must say which layers ran and name the live suite as run or not run.
=== commit-to-integration-branch

From 2026-11-08, JusPrin app work lands on `jusprin-dev`. Kenneth: "branch out a jusprin-dev from the upstream merge commit, and use this branch as the dev branch". It starts at `975c703f08` (the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 into ui-walkthrough) and contains `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those. AGENTS.md's "Branches" section records this. `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1. Server code in tsd-enterprise goes straight to `master` (2026-11-06 rule, unchanged).

History: 2026-11-06 `jusprin-newui-integration`; 2026-11-07 `ui-walkthrough`; 2026-11-08 `jusprin-dev`.

`main`, Kenneth 2026-11-08: "main will be the stable branch that doesn't allow force push ( except in some extreme circumstances when no other options are feasible). This is so that the users who clone our repo won't have to force pull." and "for now, it also double a release branch. But this rule is more flexible than the first one." GitHub branch protection on `main` blocks force pushes and deletion, admins included (enforce_admins). `main` moves forward from `jusprin-dev` only when a version is released; ask before fast-forwarding it. On 2026-11-08 Kenneth chose to leave `main` at 4da9d7beb4 until 2.0.0 ships, although that means the scheduled nightly keeps running `main`'s older file and doesn't build `jusprin-dev` until then. Start the nightly by hand on `jusprin-dev` with only `-f sign_macos=true`. GitHub runs scheduled workflows from `main`'s copy of the file, and validates dispatch inputs against it.

**Why:** the dev branch is the build Kenneth reviews; work on a side branch never reaches what he tests.

**How to apply:** Kenneth, 2026-11-08: "I want the main checkout to be always on jusprin-dev". Since then /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin holds `jusprin-dev`; byoai-newui was moved to its own branch `byoai-newui`. Git allows one checkout per branch, so never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. Commit from a worktree of your own on its own branch or detached at the tip. Then bring the main checkout along so its files match the branch; moving the ref from elsewhere (update-ref, or a push without a pull) leaves the main checkout's `git status` showing the new commits as reversed. When pushing is asked: push to origin jusprin-dev, then `git -C /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin pull --ff-only` (Kenneth: "you just need to bring the local main checkout by pulling from the remote"). Push nothing unless asked. Supersedes the landing question in [[merge-no-ff-not-squash]].
=== no-merge-commits-on-jusprin-dev

Kenneth, 2026-11-11, when asked whether to merge claude/plan-ends-line (one commit) into jusprin-dev: "Are you going to create a merge commit? I hate a very noisy branch with a lot of merge commits."

The same day the main session missed that side-thread answer and landed it with `git merge --no-ff` (8838af0820) and pushed it. With Kenneth's yes it was replaced by the plain commit 12e1529cb6 (force-push with lease) minutes later.

**Why:** jusprin-dev's history is what Kenneth reads; merge commits for one-commit branches are noise.

**How to apply:** land a branch on jusprin-dev as plain commits (cherry-pick, or rebase then fast-forward). Before landing, check side threads (btw forks of this session) for anything Kenneth said about how to land. Ask only if the branch is long enough that a merge commit might be wanted. Refines [[merge-no-ff-not-squash]] and [[commit-to-integration-branch]].
=== tool-error-contract

Kenneth chose the full contract (option a) for tool errors on 2026-10-21. Implemented as one commit, 29ae944fea, on branch `claude/tool-error-contract` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-error-contract`, cut from bed54fd8fe). Fast-forwarded onto `jusprin-newui` the same day and pushed. The branch and worktree were deleted after the merge; the follow-up 9ad6bb927f (workspace_inspect shows disabled copies) sits on top.

His answers to the five open decisions:
- D2: no `changed` or `next` fields in the error envelope. Messages carry the outcome.
- D3: one spelling of each code on both surfaces; MCP no longer renames codes.
- D4: a busy OrcaSlicer keeps failing (`busy`); the tool does not wait.
- D5: `local_save_failed` stays a failure even when the change ran.
- D6: report partial changes in the message (no rollback); prefer checking before changing.

**Why:** a code that means one next step, truthful about what changed, is what a model can act on; the old `unavailable_operation` → `workspace_unavailable` rename told MCP clients JusPrin was closed.

**How to apply:** a new failure picks a code from `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp` (`fail()` throws on any other), and an "impossible" state throws instead of failing. Don't propose `changed`/`next` fields again. Background and inventory: the untracked `tool-error-reporting-sweep.md` in the main checkout. Related: [[rare-failures-get-a-generic-error]], [[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].

content.content:
=== jusprin-worktree-build

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
=== agent-setup-api-key-path

Commit `d4012fe1df` on `jusprin-newui` (2026-09-01) built the API-key route of
Agent setup, the destination of the previously inert "Set up the agent" button
from `454e9a1b5f`. Design came from the Figma file **JusPrin v2**, page
"Agent Setup - Empty State" (5 frames); since 2026-10-20 the up-to-date version of that page is the
"Agent Setup · Empty State" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas artifact ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]). See [[agent-bridge-phase-5]] for the
preceding phase.

**Verification and construction are the same act.** `ProviderKeySetup` checks a
key by running one real request through the same `OpenAIResponsesAgent` the
Agent will use, and hands that already-connected instance back as the outcome.
A key that passes cannot drift apart from an Agent that works, and the
"replied in 0.8 s" shown is the measurement that happened. Prefer this over a
separate validation call if this is ever extended to another provider.

**The probe carries no project data.** It sends a fixed sentence and an empty
workspace snapshot: a provider the user has not chosen yet must not receive
their workspace just to prove a key works. A test asserts this.

Structure: setup is poll-driven like `IAgentService` so `AgentHost` stays
deterministic; the probe is GUI-free and unit-testable; the commit step
(AppConfig only; the key is `jusprin_agent.openai_api_key` since 2026-09-14, moved out of the Keychain because every unsigned rebuild re-prompted) is injected from `AgentConfiguration.cpp`, which is also
where completing the flow records `cloud_consent`. Threaded through as
`AgentRuntime::setup`. Protocol grew `setup_check_key` / `setup_cancel` /
`setup_status` under an `agent_setup` capability, no version bump — see
[[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].

**Deliberately not built, in priority order:** an Anthropic adapter (so the
design's default tab is disabled and the screen opens on OpenAI); the "Other…"
provider (meaning undefined); "Continue with JusPrin" (no account backend
exists in the repo — needs the auth endpoint, flow shape, and whether the app
receives a JusPrin token or a provider key); "Run a model on this machine"
(needs a JusPrin MCP server that may not exist, and a download source to
confirm before writing code that fetches a binary).

Testing this path: the shell harness points `JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` at a
closed local port so the real host, page, and HTTP transport are exercised
without an external service — that covers the failure path only. For a real
key, `--manual-unconfigured` (see [[jusprin-shell-manual-harness]]). The key now lives in the harness's AppConfig, so it does not survive runs;
an old `JusPrin Agent OpenAI` Keychain entry is ignored.
=== api-key-saved-state

Built from the canvas board "api-key-field · saved vs empty · proposal" (Agent Setup · Empty State page). Committed 2026-10-21 as 2d19270c49 on jusprin-newui (fast-forward from f073fdba96), pushed the same day.

- Capability `saved_keys`: host→page `setup_keys {keys:[{provider,hint,rejected}]}`, page→host `setup_remove_key {provider}`. Hint = `api_key_hint()` in AgentSetup.cpp: a fixed per-provider prefix table + "…" + last 4, tail hidden unless ≥8 chars stay hidden.
- Remove: AppConfig item erased and saved at once; if it was the recorded `provider`, that moves to the first provider still holding a key; host rebuilds the agent from the model source (or goes Unavailable when none left).
- **"Rejected" is my interpretation, not Kenneth's:** the board shows a check of the saved key, but nothing checks a saved key today. I chose: a chat turn whose provider answers `invalid_credentials` (401/403) marks that provider's key rejected, in memory, keyed by hint so a replaced key clears it. No auto-probe on screen open (would cost a live call each open). The printer-panel host (no model source) cannot attribute a refusal and never marks one.
- Key field = Field/Secret (Kenneth, 2026-10-21): `--field-height` 26, `--field-padding-x` 8, value in code, placeholder body / text-secondary as Field/Text draws it; actions are Button/Link. Board rebuilt to match by `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_key_states.py` (board now 962 tall, canvas version 44).

Related: [[agent-setup-api-key-path]], [[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]], [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]].
=== agent-setup-one-flow-decisions

Decided 2026-10-23 in a design session; the full document is the untracked `agent-setup-flow-decisions.md` in
the main checkout root (never committed). Context: JusPrin's own Preferences window landed on jusprin-newui as
641c17f13e (modal over any screen, Agent section draws the same key/tool rows as setup, shell reloads the docked
agent on close if `jusprin_agent` changed).

Kenneth's decisions:
1. Preferences › Agent is the one setup flow, first time included. The in-pane chooser, the printer panel's
   in-body chooser, the print-issue MessageDialog ("Set up now / Not now"), `open_agent_setup`/`request_setup`
   and `AgentPageMode::EmbeddedSetup` are to go. The first-run setup boards on the canvas page "Agent setup &
   Preferences" are history.
2. No separate question. Each surface shows its own not-set-up state with one action that opens Preferences ›
   Agent: the print-issue bubble draws one button "Set up the agent…" (Kenneth chose "agent" over "assistant") instead of Ask AI / Resolve with AI;
   the pane and printer panel keep their "No agent connected" offer and setup bar; calibration's board-3
   Confirmation adds one sentence and its primary button reads "Set up the agent…".
3. When the window closes with an agent, the surface resumes with the agent live; nothing is sent for the
   person (bubble shows its two buttons; confirmation's button becomes "Start test"; panel greeting continues).
4. Cancel changes nothing underneath; the pending choice stays where it was; the printer panel is never closed
   on the person's behalf.
5. The pane keeps its own entry (offer, setup bar, chat list row), each opening Preferences › Agent.

**Why:** three different answers to "needs the agent, none set up" existed and calibration would add a fourth;
Kenneth: "On the homepage, most users don't have a workspace open. So we just randomly open a new workspace?"
The Agent pane does not exist on Home (force-collapsed in `on_page_changed`), so only a window over Home works.

**How to apply:** any new entry point that needs the Agent follows rule 2 to 4; never add a chooser inside a
pane or a MessageDialog. Implementation detail noted: the printer panel builds its runtime at `open()` and must
reload it after Preferences closes. Related: [[calibration-design-decisions]], [[agent-setup-api-key-path]],
[[api-key-saved-state]], [[use-orca-messagedialog]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]].

Canvas (2026-10-23): board "Agent setup · one door" on the "Agent setup & Preferences" page and board 3b on "Calibration · Printer & Filament" draw these states; builder `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_no_agent_boards.py`. With no provider set up, the composer's model picker shows the raw id "gpt-5.4-mini" (default provider openai, empty catalogue) and no thinking picker; Kenneth asked for it drawn.
=== expected-errors-tables-confirmed

- Sign-in ended, or own API key rejected → "Their sign-in has ended, or the API key was rejected." → Sign in again, or update the key
- Out of credits → "They are out of credits." → Get more credits
- Chat larger than the AI service accepts → "The request was too large for the AI service." → none shown today
- Provider or our server limiting speed → "The AI service is rate limited." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider overloaded → "The AI service is overloaded." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider down or unreachable from our server → "The AI service is temporarily unavailable." → Retry
- Provider too slow, or connection stalled → "The AI request timed out." → Retry
- No network → "The AI request could not reach the service." → Check the network, then Retry

- Signed out → "Sign in to JusPrin to continue." → Sign in again

- Too many turns a minute, or provider limiting us → "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again." → Wait and retry
- Server's slots for large requests all taken → "JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment." → Retry
- Provider down, overloaded or unreachable → "The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly." → Retry
- Provider too slow → "The model service took too long to answer." → Retry
- Chat or report photos too large → "The request is too large." → New chat, or fewer pictures
- Print report too short → "A report needs a few sentences." → Write more
- Print report has no photo → "A report needs a photo of the printed object." → Add a photo

content.content:
On 2026-10-19 the batch-B headline journeys pointed the real in-app agent at
OpenRouter's /responses with deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu, AtlasCloud. The first request after a model load carries the
plate picture (file-loaded skill) and failed with HTTP 404 "No endpoints found
that support image input"; the app reports any unhandled status as
"network_error: could not reach the OpenAI service", which hides this.

**How to apply:** a live journey on those hosts must drop `input_image`
parts (and items left empty) from the body, as tests/project_prompt's runner
does; say in the report that the model never saw the pictures. The runner is
the uncommitted `--plan-journey` harness mode, saved as
plan-journey-harness-mode.patch in the side-session notes folder of session
local_2012258e. Related: [[model-probe-live-chat-harness]],
[[prompt-eval-spend-budget]].

Branch `claude/state-guidance` (worktree cool-bardeen-7f40f5), three commits on local jusprin-newui 77115d05b3, not pushed; report untracked at the worktree root as state-guidance-report.md.

What it does:
- `AgentHost::make_agent_request` renders the active plate (default `RenderRequest`, same as view_render) on the file-open turn when the plate has a printable object, as `AgentRequest::picture`; `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` sends it as the last `input_image` part of the user message. Rendered when the request is built, never stored or replayed.
- `AgentRequest::state_note` goes out as a trailing `{"role":"developer"}` item (the last item). Built in C++ only when no setup title and no intent fields: "Nothing is recorded yet about what this print is for. [The picture is the plate as loaded.] Once its purpose is known, check the filament and process presets against that purpose."
- `intent_update` result gains required `unchecked`: "Not yet checked against the recorded purpose: printer preset X, filament preset Y, process preset Z, plate type W." (coordinator, `unchecked_against_purpose`).
- Eval: petg-restated cases deleted (same as Kenneth's uncommitted main-checkout change), `after-intent` case added (record on the presets_list reply in `prepare`), recorder checks the file-note opening turn for picture + note, requests.json re-recorded (23 points). The file-note-not-instructions case does NOT carry the picture: its point is the turn after.
- Slice-with-warnings and print-issue notes judged unnecessary: slice_start's description and Preparing already send the model to slice_report; the <print_issue> block already carries the issue.

**Why:** Kenneth approved both the picture and the state notes on 2026-10-16 following the published-practice argument (harness-supplied, last-in-request guidance beats standing rules).
**How to apply:** the proposed live batch (7 cases x 3 runs, ~650k input tokens, plus a same-day before run from jusprin-newui) is in the report and needs Kenneth's approval. Tool-description or result changes require regenerating project_tools.json (`JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`) and re-recording. Related: [[project-prompt-harness-ported]], [[print-setup-prompt-cases]], [[rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs]], [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]].

The search turned up enough to answer, with one naming mismatch to check.

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/models` takes no request parameters. This endpoint has no request parameters.
- **`loaded_instances`:** The docs describe it as the list of currently loaded instances of a model, and each entry has an `id` and a `config` object. loaded_instances : array List of currently loaded instances of this model. id : string Unique identifier for the loaded model instance. config : object Configuration for the loaded instance. Per a third-party summary, that config holds settings such as context length and GPU offload. loaded_instances: Array of currently loaded instances with their specific config (context length, GPU offload, etc.).
- **`context_length` vs. `max_context_length`:** The example payloads use `max_context_length`, not `context_length`, at the model level. One example shows "max_context_length": 131072. So the field you're looking for is probably `max_context_length`, and the per-instance loaded context may sit inside `loaded_instances[].config`. I couldn't confirm the exact key name inside `config`.
- **`capabilities`:** The object holds boolean flags. One documented example lists "vision": false, "trained_for_tool_use": true, and a third-party summary describes them as boolean flags for vision, trained_for_tool_use, and reasoning settings. A bug report asks for reasoning to be exposed, which suggests it wasn't reliably present at that version. Expose reasoning/thinking capabilities for the models that provides it
- **Older API differs:** The v0 API used a list rather than flags. The OpenAI‑compatible REST API (/api/v0) now returns a capabilities array in the GET /models response. Each model lists its supported capabilities (e.g. "tool_use"). Don't mix the two shapes.
- **Version:** The v1 API arrived with LM Studio 0.4.0. With LM Studio 0.4.0, we have officially released our native v1 REST API at /api/v1/* endpoints and recommend using it.

Recommendation: confirm the exact `config` keys against a live response from your LM Studio version, since the docs I found don't show a full `loaded_instances` example.

I need the exact JSON shape of GET /api/v1/models: the top-level key holding the models list, each model's key names for its id (the identifier used as "model" in /v1/responses or /v1/chat/completions), type (llm vs embedding), capabilities (vision, trained_for_tool_use) and loaded_instances; and the exact key name for the loaded instance's context length inside loaded_instances[].config. Quote a full example response verbatim if the page has one. Also say what the docs say the default context length is when a model is loaded just in time by a request (JIT loading), if stated.

content.text: <tools-used-before-summary>WebFetch</tools-used-before-summary>

The list page gives the key names you need. Its full example response is too long for me to reproduce verbatim here, because both pages are from a non-preapproved source and my quoting limit is 125 characters. The key names below are taken directly from the page's field list and example.

**Top-level key:** `models`, an array of model objects.

**Per-model keys:**
- **Model identifier:** `key` (string), described as "Unique identifier for the model." Example from the page: `"google/gemma-4-26b-a4b"`. The page does not explicitly say this value is what goes in the `model` field of `/v1/responses` or `/v1/chat/completions`. The load page's `model` parameter is described as the "Unique identifier for the model to load," which suggests the same value works. The `variants` array can also list names such as `"google/gemma-4-26b-a4b@q4_k_m"`, and the page does not say which form to use.
- **Type:** `type`, one of `"llm"`, `"embedding"`, or `"decision"`.
- **Capabilities:** `capabilities` is an object containing `vision` (boolean) and `trained_for_tool_use` (boolean). It is absent for embedding and decision models. It can also contain a `reasoning` object.
- **Loaded instances:** `loaded_instances`, an array of objects with `id` (string) and `config` (object). It is an empty array when the model is not loaded.

**Context length:** `loaded_instances[].config.context_length` (number, "The maximum context length for the model in number of tokens"). The model-level `max_context_length` is a separate field and is not the loaded instance's value.

**JIT default context length:** The pages do not state one. The load page says `context_length` is optional and "Maximum number of tokens that the model will consider," but it does not say what value applies when the field is omitted or when a request triggers JIT loading.

Sources read:
- https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/rest/list
- https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/rest/load

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Where to Create Worktrees and Temporary Folders

This file is read by more than one coding tool, so each rule names the idea first and the tool-specific path second.

1. **Use the location your own tool already uses for worktrees.** Claude Code: `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`. Codex: `~/.codex/worktrees/`. If this session was started inside a worktree the tool created, put any further worktree beside it.
2. **Never create a worktree or a working folder in `~` or directly under `~/Projects`.** That includes sibling folders such as `<repo>-worktrees`. This holds for a different repo than the one the session started in: use that repo's tool-managed location (rule 1) or the scratch directory (rule 3).
3. **Short-lived worktrees, build output, logs, screenshots and scripts go in the session's scratch or temp directory** if the tool gives one (Claude Code names it in the session instructions). If it gives none, use a new folder under the system temp directory, not the home directory.
4. **Keep non-worktree files out of worktree folders.** Logs, screenshots and scripts do not belong beside the worktrees. They go in the scratch directory, or inside the one worktree they concern.
5. **Use absolute paths when creating a worktree.** A shell may reset its working directory between commands, and a path starting with `~` or `..` can land somewhere unintended.
6. **Say where it is.** After creating a worktree, tell the user its full path, and remove it and its branch when the work is finished and merged.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Branches

- `jusprin-dev` is the development branch. Start each change on a new branch from it and land the change there. It began at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains the earlier development branches `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those.
- `main` is the stable branch and GitHub's default branch: the repository's front page, its issue forms, and the workflows GitHub runs on a schedule come from it.
  - Never force-push `main`, so that people who cloned the repository never have to force-pull. Only in an extreme case with no other way out, and with Kenneth's yes, may an admin lift the GitHub protection that blocks force pushes and deletion.
  - For now `main` is also the release branch: it moves forward from `jusprin-dev` when a version is released, and releases are built from it. This may change if a separate release branch is added later.
- `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1, for fixes to that version only.
- `jusprin-v2-poc` holds the experiments described below.
- Take each OrcaSlicer release into `jusprin-dev` as `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` rule 10 describes.

## Releasing

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds a release into a draft on GitHub; its top comment says how to start it. It refuses the commit until it has all of these:

- The version, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`, above every released JusPrin version.
- The release notes, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`.
- The Sentry secrets: `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, the project the app sends error reports and crashes to, and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`, which upload each build's debug files and the pages' source maps. A platform's build fails unless Sentry then holds debug information with file and line for the app's own code (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh`) and a source map for each page as built (`sentry_page_maps.sh` beside it); the nightly build checks the same.
- The guide, `docs/guide/`, checked for that version. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` on a built copy of the commit, fix every page it reports, and commit the pages with their pictures, skills and `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`, as `docs/guide/README.md` describes under "Before a release". That file names the version the check last passed for, not the commit. Ticking "Release without the guide check" on the workflow's Run workflow form skips this, and the draft's title then says so. A release started by pushing a `jusprin-release/` branch has no form, so it always needs the file.

## Error handling

Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."

The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.

### Two kinds of failure

A condition we can name in advance, and that the person can act on, is an expected error. It is designed for when the feature is built, like any other part of the feature, once we have verified how it shows up: from the other side's documentation or a real answer, not from memory.

Everything else is a surprise, an unexpected error. No handling is written for it, it stops the work, and it is reported with everything known. The reporting must be complete, because a surprise that is not reported is lost. A failure that ends in a log line alone, a default value, or a sentence for "anything else" is a hole. Reading the code can check this: from each place work starts, follow a failure up to the handler that reports it.

Reports then show which surprises to fix, and which are really conditions that need a design.

Every failure is written to the log, expected or unexpected. The log is kept as well as the report, never in its place.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

### Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.

## Build Commands

Build the Release configuration unless asked otherwise.

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config Release --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config Release --target all --

# Windows
cmake --build . --config Release --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.
- Before building against a dependency folder built earlier, such as the main checkout's `deps/build/arm64`, run `scripts/deps_current.sh <folder>`. It rebuilds the libraries whose `deps/` recipe changed since that folder was built.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/`; see [tests/AGENTS.md](tests/AGENTS.md) for where a new test belongs and the conventions to follow.

```bash
cd build && ctest -C Release --output-on-failure    # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r -C Release       # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print -C Release
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Documentation

- Docs live in `docs/`; the high-level design of a subsystem goes in `docs/HLSD/<subsystem>.md`.
- Describe the design as it stands — what the subsystem does, why it exists, and the constraints that shape it. Not the route that got there: no phases, task lists, status markers, or "before/after this PR" framing.
- Planning and investigation output (brainstorms, superpowers design and plan docs) stays in `docs/superpowers/`, which is gitignored. Never commit it.
- Write a doc only when the design is not evident from the code, and when a change invalidates an existing one, update it in the same PR.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Include what you use: include the header for every symbol a file uses, and keep headers compilable on their own. Never rely on the precompiled header or a transitive include. The `clang-tidy` CI job enforces this on changed lines; run the same check locally with `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` (`scripts\run_clang_tidy.ps1` on Windows), which sets up everything it needs
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.
- Always use `SetSizerAndFit(sizer)` instead of `SetSizer(sizer)` on top level window. Unless `SetSizer` must be called before the full layout is built, call `sizer->SetSizeHints(window)` afterwards in this case.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.

- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Before designing a screen or writing any on-screen text, follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md`: whole-screen boards with real strings, the wording rule, and a cold-reader check on screenshots before and after building.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Pull requests

Before opening a pull request or posting on GitHub, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), including its "If you are an AI agent" section.

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
- For profile changes (`resources/profiles/<Vendor>/**`), check that `version` in the sibling `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` was bumped.
- For new or changed UI strings, check they follow [Writing translatable strings in the source](#writing-translatable-strings-in-the-source): no concatenated fragments, plural forms for counts, contexts for ambiguous words.
- For translation changes (`localization/i18n/**/*.po`), check that recurring terms match the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) for that language.

## Localization & translations

Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.

### Writing translatable strings in the source

Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:

- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.

See `.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/source-audit.md` for the full checklist.

### Terminology

- Use the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) as the source of truth for recurring terms, so the same English term is always rendered the same way within a language, and terms that must stay in English (brand/product names, acronyms, materials, file formats, G-code tokens, macros/variables/identifiers) are not translated.
- If a term's established translation changes, update both the affected `.po` files and the glossary (`developer_reference/glossary/<lang>.tsv` in the wiki, then regenerate) so they stay in sync.
- Translate the *meaning*, not the words. Check what the string actually controls before translating it — English reuses one word for different things. `Flow ratio` (multiplier), `Flow Rate` (throughput) and `Flow Dynamics` (pressure compensation) are three different terms; `extruder` may mean the toolhead, the feeder motor, or the nozzle depending on the string.
- Reuse one template per recurring message shape (`Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?`), even where the English wording varies.

### Editing rules

- Only edit `msgstr` — **never** change `msgid`, and never "fix" wrong English in the translation alone. Report the source string instead.
- Preserve exactly: placeholders (`%s`, `%d`, `%1%`, `%zu`, `%%`), every `\n` (count *and* position, including leading/trailing), leading/trailing spaces, HTML tags, `℃`, and the file's encoding and line endings.
- **Never reorder positional arguments** in a `c-format` string. If the msgid is `%d` then `%s`, that order must hold — swapping them breaks at runtime.
- `msgctxt` separates homonyms — always read it. `Back`/`Camera View` is the rear view of the 3D navigator, while `Back`/`Navigation` is the go-back button; `Top` exists in the *Alignment*, *Layers* and *Camera View* senses.
- When a string needs disambiguating, add context in the source (`_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`), don't work around it in the translation.
- A literal `%` inside a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format` will fail `msgfmt`. Fix it with a `// xgettext:no-c-format, no-boost-format` comment above the string in the source — do not mangle the translation or use `%%` in text that is never passed through printf.
- Plural entries: read `nplurals` from the catalog's `Plural-Forms` header (it is **not** always 2 — ja/ko/zh/th/vi use 1, ru/cs/pl/lt use 3, uk uses 4). Each form must be genuinely inflected for its quantity; repeating one sentence across all forms is a bug in Slavic/Baltic languages, though it is correct for Turkish and Hungarian.
- An entry whose `msgstr` equals its `msgid` is untranslated even though it is not empty; a plural entry with any empty form is likewise incomplete.
- Mark machine-produced translations with an `# AI Translated` translator comment. Don't add it to a human translation you didn't actually rewrite.
- When you can't be sure of a machine translation's meaning or UI wording, also add `# Needs human review: <what to check>`. Never use `fuzzy` for this — fuzzy entries are hidden from users.
- Don't reflow or re-wrap unrelated entries — keep the diff limited to the strings you changed.

### Verifying

- `scripts/run_gettext.bat --full` (Windows) regenerates the template, merges every catalog and compiles the `.mo` files. It must exit 0.
- Or check a single catalog with `msgfmt --check-format --check-header -o <out>.mo localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`. Without `--check-header`, msgfmt skips the placeholder check in plural forms.
- Fuzzy entries are not shown to users. If you correct one, clear its `fuzzy` flag, otherwise the fix never ships.

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands

4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

## Where to Create Worktrees and Temporary Folders

This file is read by more than one coding tool, so each rule names the idea first and the tool-specific path second.

3. **Short-lived worktrees, build output, logs, screenshots and scripts go in the session's scratch or temp directory** if the tool gives one (Claude Code names it in the session instructions). If it gives none, use a new folder under the system temp directory, not the home directory.
4. **Keep non-worktree files out of worktree folders.** Logs, screenshots and scripts do not belong beside the worktrees. They go in the scratch directory, or inside the one worktree they concern.

Before writing any fix:

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
