entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m -q --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

87:## Use a model on this computer
88-
89-A model you run yourself with Ollama, LM Studio or a similar app costs nothing, and your messages go to that app instead of an online AI service. Local models are slower and make more mistakes than the cloud ones.
90-
91-1. Start Ollama or LM Studio, with a model downloaded. In LM Studio, turn on its local server.
92-2. In Preferences, open **BYOAI**. Under **A model on this computer**, click **Set up**.
93-3. The address is Ollama's. For LM Studio, change it to `http://127.0.0.1:1234`. Click **Find models**.
94-4. Pick a model and click **Use this model**. JusPrin sends it one real request with all the app's tools, which can take a minute the first time. **Change** and **Remove** change it later.
95-
96-The model must support tools, and the app must run it with a context length of at least 32k:
97-
98-- In Ollama, `ollama show <model>` lists `tools` under Capabilities when the model has them. Set the context length with the slider in the Ollama app's settings, or start Ollama with `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768 ollama serve`.
99-- In LM Studio, set the context length in the model's load settings before it loads, or load it with `lms load <model> --context-length 32768`. A model loaded already has to be loaded again.
100-
101-A model that can't see pictures works too, but AI then works without seeing your model. New chats keep starting with the model they started with before; choose the local model beside a new chat's message box, or under **New chats start with** in **BYOAI**.

109-1. In Preferences, open **BYOAI**. Under **Connect an AI tool you already use**, each tool says whether it was found on this computer. **Look again** searches again.

111-3. When it says **Connected**, click **Done**. The tool can now see and change the open project.

content.content:
## What the command does

1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4. `components/Guide.test.tsx` checks that the app's guide window lists every page and shows each with all its pictures and without the parts written for AI.
4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

## Writing a page

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it. The model reads every page's description together in one list, and the Claude command-line tool that `--ask-ai` runs through cuts a tool description longer than about 2,000 characters, so keep each one short: about 200 bytes. Write `...` rather than `…` in it, since that tool rewrites the one as the other.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- A picture is kept at twice the screen's size, and the guide window shows it at half, the size it has on screen. Mark a run's picture that the harness draws at the screen's own size with `"atScreenSize": true`, and the command doubles it.

content.text:
Local models are built and work in the real app with Ollama. You can set up a model from Preferences › BYOAI, and chats then run on it. All tests pass, and nothing is committed.

**What I tested in the real app.** I used a copy of the new build with its own settings folder, the API keys and sign-in removed, and the Ollama running on this Mac:
- **Find models:** listed qwen3.5:9b ("Can see pictures") and llama3.2 ("Can't see pictures…") in 0.15 seconds.
- **Use this model:** passed for llama3.2 in 23 seconds and for qwen3.5:9b in 47 seconds. The settings file then held the address, model, runtime and picture flag. With no other provider set up, the local model became the default, as designed.
- **Remove:** cleared all of it.
- **Wrong address:** typing `127.0.0.1:9` showed your approved sentence: "Nothing is answering at 127.0.0.1:9. Start Ollama or LM Studio, then try again."
- **A real chat:** opening an STL started a chat on qwen3.5:9b. The request carried the plate picture. The model used two of the app's tools (it analysed the object and rendered the plate) and gave a sensible summary of the part.

**Two bugs the run found, both fixed with a test that fails on the old code:**
- **Web search:** the model on this computer was told "You have web_search" but got no such tool. The page now also sends its instructions without that paragraph, and a provider with no web search gets that copy. Cloud providers get byte-identical instructions to before, so the prompt suite isn't affected. The guide now says local models can't search the web.
- **Change:** while changing to another model, the row said "Not set up" even though the saved model is still what chats use. It now keeps showing the saved model.

**Also done:**
- All 22 languages are translated (37 new strings each), marked "# AI Translated".
- The message list shared by the page and the app now includes the new local-model messages.
- Every file now includes what it uses directly; the include check passes on all 28 changed files.
- Results: 648 native agent tests pass, 845 page tests pass, and the guide checks pass.

**Not tested live:**
- LM Studio, which is tested only against recorded answers.
- A model with too small a context. Ollama itself loaded llama3.2 with a 32k context, so it passed.

Decision needed: these sentences weren't on the approved boards, and they need your yes because they're what people read:
- **Old chat, model removed:** "This chat ran on a model on this computer that is no longer set up. Set it up again in the AI settings to continue it, or start a new chat."
- **No models found:** "Ollama at … has no models. Download one in Ollama, then find models again.", with the same sentence for LM Studio and "that app".
- **Unknown app:** "The app at …" lines, and "…its context length in the app that runs it must be at least 32k."
- **Model menu:** "Ollama · no credits", and "No credits" when the app is unknown.
- **Unknown app's label:** "this computer".
- **The guide:** its new "Use a model on this computer" section.

The other option is to change any of them before commit; each change also means redoing that string's 22 translations. My pick is to approve them as they are. Do you approve all of them, or do you want to edit some?

content: Approve all

From 2026-11-08, JusPrin app work lands on `jusprin-dev`. Kenneth: "branch out a jusprin-dev from the upstream merge commit, and use this branch as the dev branch". It starts at `975c703f08` (the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 into ui-walkthrough) and contains `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those. AGENTS.md's "Branches" section records this. `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1. Server code in tsd-enterprise goes straight to `master` (2026-11-06 rule, unchanged).

History: 2026-11-06 `jusprin-newui-integration`; 2026-11-07 `ui-walkthrough`; 2026-11-08 `jusprin-dev`.

`main`, Kenneth 2026-11-08: "main will be the stable branch that doesn't allow force push ( except in some extreme circumstances when no other options are feasible). This is so that the users who clone our repo won't have to force pull." and "for now, it also double a release branch. But this rule is more flexible than the first one." GitHub branch protection on `main` blocks force pushes and deletion, admins included (enforce_admins). `main` moves forward from `jusprin-dev` only when a version is released; ask before fast-forwarding it. On 2026-11-08 Kenneth chose to leave `main` at 4da9d7beb4 until 2.0.0 ships, although that means the scheduled nightly keeps running `main`'s older file and doesn't build `jusprin-dev` until then. Start the nightly by hand on `jusprin-dev` with only `-f sign_macos=true`. GitHub runs scheduled workflows from `main`'s copy of the file, and validates dispatch inputs against it.

**Why:** the dev branch is the build Kenneth reviews; work on a side branch never reaches what he tests.

**How to apply:** Kenneth, 2026-11-08: "I want the main checkout to be always on jusprin-dev". Since then /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin holds `jusprin-dev`; byoai-newui was moved to its own branch `byoai-newui`. Git allows one checkout per branch, so never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. Commit from a worktree of your own on its own branch or detached at the tip. Then bring the main checkout along so its files match the branch; moving the ref from elsewhere (update-ref, or a push without a pull) leaves the main checkout's `git status` showing the new commits as reversed. When pushing is asked: push to origin jusprin-dev, then `git -C /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin pull --ff-only` (Kenneth: "you just need to bring the local main checkout by pulling from the remote"). Push nothing unless asked. Supersedes the landing question in [[merge-no-ff-not-squash]].

Kenneth, 2026-11-11, when asked whether to merge claude/plan-ends-line (one commit) into jusprin-dev: "Are you going to create a merge commit? I hate a very noisy branch with a lot of merge commits."

The same day the main session missed that side-thread answer and landed it with `git merge --no-ff` (8838af0820) and pushed it. With Kenneth's yes it was replaced by the plain commit 12e1529cb6 (force-push with lease) minutes later.

**Why:** jusprin-dev's history is what Kenneth reads; merge commits for one-commit branches are noise.

**How to apply:** land a branch on jusprin-dev as plain commits (cherry-pick, or rebase then fast-forward). Before landing, check side threads (btw forks of this session) for anything Kenneth said about how to land. Ask only if the branch is long enough that a merge commit might be wanted. Refines [[merge-no-ff-not-squash]] and [[commit-to-integration-branch]].

On 2026-10-08 a session running in `.claude/worktrees/<name>` tried to write a report next to its handoff in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/` and the Write tool was refused by a hook: edits to the base checkout "do not land on this session's branch and may corrupt the user's primary working copy". Bash `cp` is not stopped by the hook, but that is working around a deliberate guard, so anything copied there was moved back.

**Why:** handoffs are read from the main checkout ([[handoff-docs-not-committed]]), which makes it tempting to hand the report back in the same place.

**How to apply:** write reports and evidence folders in the worktree root, leave them untracked ([[temp-docs-stay-untracked-and-visible]]), and give Kenneth the worktree path. Never use the scratchpad for a deliverable; the app's file pane cannot open it as part of the project.

Chats can run on a model on this computer, in Ollama or LM Studio

Preferences › BYOAI has a new group, "A model on this computer". The person
enters the address of the app that runs the model (Ollama's is filled in),
the app lists that app's models with whether each can see pictures, and
"Use this model" checks the one picked before saving it. The check sends
one real request with every tool the chat offers, then asks the app what
context it loaded the model with; a model passes when it answers and its
context is at least 32k. The model then appears under "On this computer"
in each chat's model menu, as "Ollama · no credits". Change looks at the
same address again; Remove forgets the address and model.

How it works:
- A new provider row, "local", sends OpenAI's Responses API to the address
  the person entered (/v1/responses), with no key, no cloud consent, no
  request time limit and no web search.
- LocalModelSetup finds the models (Ollama's /api/show and LM Studio's
  /api/v1/models say which take tools and pictures) and runs the check.
  Its tests replay Ollama 0.40.17's real answers.
- The address, model, app and picture flag are kept in the jusprin_agent
  settings. A local model becomes the default for chats only when no other
  provider is set up.
- A model that cannot see pictures gets none: attached pictures, plate
  pictures from skills and pictures in tool results are left out, and the
  model is told no picture is attached.
- The model is not told it has web search. The page now sends each chat's
  instructions also without the paragraph that offers web search, and a
  provider with no web search gets that copy. Cloud providers get the same
  text as before.
- New page and host messages: local_find, local_check, local_cancel,
  local_remove and local_status, and the "local_model" capability.

The two errors the person can act on are new expected errors. Kenneth
approved both sentences on 2026-11-24: "Approve both", and that the first
shows the address the person entered: "Yes, entered address".
- "Nothing is answering at <address>. Start Ollama or LM Studio, then try
  again."
- "This model can't run the app's tools. Pick a model with tool support and
  a context of at least 32k."
The screens follow the six approved canvas boards ("The screens are
approved, go build it"). The sentences not on the boards (a chat whose
local model was removed, an app with no models, an unknown app, "No
credits", "this computer", and the guide section) were approved on
2026-11-24: "Approve all".

The guide page "AI chats and your account" has a new section, "Use a
model on this computer", and its AI copy is rebuilt. New strings are
translated in all 22 languages and marked "# AI Translated".

Tested: 648 agent tests and 845 page tests pass, and the include check
passes. In the real app with Ollama 0.40.17: finding models, checking
qwen3.5:9b and llama3.2, Remove, the "Nothing is answering" sentence, and
a chat turn on qwen3.5:9b that used two of the app's tools and received
the plate picture. LM Studio is tested against recorded answers only.
EOF

www.obico.io's `release.sh` builds from the main checkout's working tree (blog/, docusaurus-i18n/, www/) and uploads everything to S3, so it also publishes other sessions' uncommitted edits in that checkout. On 2026-11-23 a deploy of commit 601ca3a was done from a clean `git worktree add --detach` at the pushed commit instead.

- `fix-locale-canonicals.py` and `append_translation_footer.py` import `yaml`: run them with the repo's own virtualenv, `/Users/kenneth/Projects/www.obico.io/env/bin/python3`; Homebrew python3 lacks it.
- `fix-locale-canonicals.py` reads blog/ and docusaurus-i18n/ next to itself, so it must run from the clean tree.
- Blog images: `obico-server/website/static/img/blogs` is a relative symlink to `../../../../blogs_img` (top-level repo folder). A Docusaurus copy elsewhere needs that link to resolve, or the build fails on a missing image.
- Docusaurus site for a clean build: `git -C obico-server archive origin/master website | tar -x` (release.sh `git pull`s the submodule first); symlink node_modules from the submodule.
- `rm -rf public/*` can fail with "Directory not empty" when a Finder window is open on public/ (Finder rewrites .DS_Store mid-delete). The build is done by then: rerun only the steps from `rm -rf public/*` onward, with `nvm use` first for `yarn gulp`.
- Never empty `obico-server/website/blog` or `i18n` with `find -delete`: it removes the tracked `.keep` and `i18n/.gitignore`, and release.sh's `git pull` in the submodule then refuses. Restore them with `git -C obico-server checkout -- website/blog/.keep website/i18n/.keep website/i18n/.gitignore`.
- Single-locale builds (`docusaurus build --locale X`) fail the link check on links that the all-locale release build accepts; only trust the all-locale build after `npm run clear`.
- `aws s3 sync` uploads all ~31,000 files each time (mtimes change); CloudFront invalidation finishes in a few minutes.
- Headless Playwright: PostHog drops events as a bot unless the UA is a normal Chrome UA and Chrome runs with `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled`.

Related: [[obico-blog-seo-check-location]].
  type: reference
---

Obico's SEO work is recorded in the website repository, `/Users/kenneth/Projects/www.obico.io/`: `SEO-PLAN.md` (plan and the 2026-03-30 pivot), `seo-research/seo-analysis-2026-03-30.md`, and `seo-research/seo-check-2026-11-19.md` (written by the session "Obico SEO troubleshooting content").

Result as of 2026-11-19: Google clicks to the blog fell from 27,400 (Mar 2026) to 9,320 (Oct 2026) a month; the troubleshooting guide from the 2026 SEO push gets about 14 Google clicks a month at position 25; OrcaSlicer guides kept their position but their click rate fell 29-71%. Kenneth, 2026-11-20: "I believe the result was not very promising."

**How to apply:** read these files before proposing blog or search content for Obico or JusPrin. On 2026-11-20 I proposed "pages on the Obico blog first" without having read them, and had to withdraw it. Related: [[jusprin2-funnel-data-location]], [[brainstorm-shows-hypotheses-not-a-plan]].

content.content:
---
title: "Use your own AI in JusPrin: an API key for Claude, OpenAI or OpenRouter (Grok too), or Claude Code and Codex"
date: 2026-11-23
slug: jusprin-own-ai-api-key
tags:
  - JusPrin
  - AI
  - Slicer
  - how-to
author: Kenneth Jiang
author_url: https://medium.com/@kennethjiang
author_image_url: https://www.obico.io/wwwimg/kj.jpg
description: JusPrin's AI can run on your own API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, or through an AI app you already use, such as Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code. Neither uses JusPrin credits. How to set each up, which models work, and what to check when it doesn't.
keywords:
  - JusPrin API key
  - JusPrin BYOAI
  - JusPrin Claude
  - JusPrin OpenAI
  - JusPrin OpenRouter
  - JusPrin Grok
  - JusPrin Claude Code
  - JusPrin MCP
  - AI slicer own API key
image: /img/blogs/jusprin-2/jusprin-logo.png
---

Say you already pay for AI. You have an Anthropic or OpenAI account for work, or you use Claude Code every day, and you'd rather not buy credits for one more AI. JusPrin lets you bring that AI with you.

There are two ways, and neither uses JusPrin credits:

- **Your own API key** from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter. JusPrin's chat runs on your key, and the provider bills you for what you use. Through OpenRouter that includes xAI's Grok and many other models.
- **An AI app you already use**, such as Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code. That app's AI works on the project you have open in JusPrin.

Both are set up in **Preferences › BYOAI** ("bring your own AI"). This page walks through each, step by step.

<!--truncate-->

## The three ways to use AI in JusPrin

| | JusPrin account | Your own API key | An AI app you already use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Where you talk to AI** | JusPrin's chat | JusPrin's chat | The other app, such as Claude Code |
| **Who you pay** | JusPrin, in credits | The AI provider, for what you use | Whatever you already pay for that app |
| **JusPrin credits used** | Yes | None | None |
| **Which models** | JusPrin's own, tuned for 3D printing | Any the provider offers that can use tools | The app's own |
| **Set up in** | Preferences › Account | Preferences › BYOAI | Preferences › BYOAI |

Any one of them works on its own, and you can switch at any time. You don't need a JusPrin account for either of the two ways on this page. You don't need AI at all to slice and print, either.

## Use your own API key

### 1. Get a key from the provider

| Provider | Where to make a key | The key starts with |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic (Claude) | [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/), under API keys | `sk-ant-` |
| OpenAI | [platform.openai.com/api-keys](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) | `sk-` |
| OpenRouter | [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys) | `sk-or-` |

An API key is billed separately from a ChatGPT or Claude chat subscription. Your provider account needs billing set up, or credit added, before the key works.

### 2. Add the key in JusPrin

1. Open Preferences. On a Mac, choose **Preferences** in the JusPrin menu, or press Cmd+,. On Windows and Linux, choose **Preferences** in the menu beside the **File** button, or press Ctrl+,.
2. Open **BYOAI**.
3. Under **Your own API key**, click **Add key** beside Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, and paste the key.
4. Click **Check key**. JusPrin checks the key with the provider.

The key is kept on your computer only. **Replace** and **Remove** change it later.

### 3. Pick a model and start a chat
